answer: Weight each identity by elapsed sequential work, not capital: it must keep extending a hash chain where every link needs the previous link plus the latest public randomness beacon, so extra hardware can't make one chain grow faster, the way a vine grows at its own pace. 500 fakes need 500 machines running for weeks, paying power for every head. Peers spot-check random links like tilting a crystal for a flaw; a precomputed chain fails because those beacon values didn't exist yet, and no pigment over a short chain hides missing links.
